task: #15365 GET + POST structured Cloudflare error handling review
method: Static source review only; no tests, builds, installs, staging, commits, or deploys were run.
verdict: PASS for the requested no-object-coercion and safe-rendering behavior, with a GET visibility test-coverage caveat.

evidence.detail: GET parses JSON with a null fallback. For non-OK responses it passes parsed data to extractApiErrorMessage with a human-readable fallback, then throws an Error from the extracted message. It does not stringify or render the response body.

POST parses JSON with an empty-object fallback and uses extractApiErrorMessage for non-OK responses. The catch stores error.message (or a translated fallback) in the notice rather than storing the raw response object.
The notice and last-error values are rendered as JSX text children. React escapes text children; no raw response body is injected as HTML.
Coverage includes structured {code,message}, string error, missing message fallback, and malformed error values (null, number, boolean, array, and non-string message) falling back safely.

The UI test supplies structured POST and GET errors, asserts the actionable POST message is visible, checks rendered text and captured Error arguments do not contain [object Object], and verifies malformed GET error value 42 maps to the status fallback rather than being forwarded as an object/number.

caveat: All current fetchCloudflaredStatus call sites pass silent=true (lines 499, 585, 740). The GET test verifies extraction by capturing Error constructor arguments, but does not assert a GET error notice is rendered. A non-silent invocation would render error.message through the Cloudflare notice JSX. The shared extractor implementation was not inspected because it is outside the allowed file scope; its behavior is supported here by the authorized direct tests.
